category_title: Children with expressive language difficulties and Sotos Syndrome who use persistent, roundabout communication strategies
minimal_context: Maliha is in the outdoor play area trying to share a personal story with the center director.
dialogue:
TUTOR: You ran over here to get me from the other end of the play area. What did you want to tell me?

STUDENT: Grandma fell down on the bed and …

TUTOR: And after that...

STUDENT: And... and... she... (stutters and repeats the words, appearing to struggle to find the appropriate words to express herself)

TUTOR: And after that? She...

STUDENT: (Opens her mouth but does not say any word, thinking for words)

options.A: Maintain a 'leaky, viscous, orientation to control' by letting the interaction go on and giving the child time to develop mischief before finally breaking up the escalating unruliness.
options.B: Augment tactics during the interaction, such as response promotion and disruption, and reallocate responding to options associated with contingent reinforcement.
options.C: Review a behavior tracking sheet with the child and have her count all of the positive and negative marks that are circled.
options.D: Act as a 'living auxiliary tool' and use auxiliary questions to support the child to express and communicate during the interaction.
